answer: Sybil resistance can be bought with cost curves rather than trust: make each agent post a bond that scales with the square of its declared peer degree, so a cluster of fake identities cannot cheaply reach the vertex where reputation actually concentrates. Every new node starts below the horizon of settled history, and climbing to the summit of the trust graph means paying real, slashable capital for each forged edge. An attacker's marginal puppet therefore costs more than its expected reward, and capital locked across hundreds of accounts stays visible and forfeitable.
